entry.title: Your terminal can't render LaTeX. Here's a 10-second fix for Claude Code and Codex
entry.summary:
Ask Claude Code or Codex to explain some math and your terminal shows this: H(p) = $-\sum_{i} p_{i} \log p_{i}$ That is LaTeX. A browser renders it into a clean equation. A terminal renders it into dollar-sign noise, because a TUI has no math engine to run. The more math-heavy your work (ML, statistics, optimization, proofs), the worse the output gets exactly where you need it clear.
That is the hard, unsolved path: it needs a graphics backend like Kitty or SIXEL, plus a fallback for SSH and tmux. There is a cheaper move. The model does not have to output LaTeX at all. Unicode already has most inline math: ∑, ∫, √, ≤, ≥, ∈, α, β, σ, x², pᵢ, set notation, even small matrices. A terminal renders all of it, because it is just text. So you teach the model to skip LaTeX and emit the Unicode directly: before: H(p) = $-\sum_{i} p_{i} \log p_{i}$ claude-math does exactly that. It has no runtime; it is a SKILL.md the agent loads, with a glyph cheatsheet so the mapping stays consistent. It is copy- and search-safe (plain Unicode, not the "mathematical alphanumeric" styling codepoints that break find-in-page), and the same file works in Claude Code and Codex. npx claude-math install # Claude Code
Restart your agent and math comes back as text you can read.
One caveat, stated plainly: this is a workaround, not native rendering. A dense derivation is still clearer as typeset math, and on a GUI surface that already renders LaTeX you want the LaTeX, not Unicode. claude-math is deliberately a terminal tool. Buh that fills an agent's answers, it is an immediate improvement. Repo: https://github.com/vladimirrott/claude-math If the Unicode mapping ever looks wrong, that is exactly the kind of issue I want to hear about.

entry.title: Juni: Python and C++ United in JunoEngine WebApp
entry.summary: Hello Devs!: Juni – a Python-feel systems language that compiles to WASM for games built on a custom software called JunoEngine URL https://junoengine.netlify.app The Hotpockets I built Juni, a statically typed systems language that aims for Python-level readability with C++-ish control: no GC, explicit memory/refs, and a compiler that targets WebAssembly. Juno is the repo around it — browser IDE, Tauri desktop shell, and a small game/sim runtime. Why I wanted one language that could author game logic and run it in the browser without a JS/TS game-script layer as the source of truth. Juni compiles to WASM; the host is a thin JS runtime (Canvas2D, WebGPU 3D, input, audio, ECS scenes). What’s in the box (v9.2) Compiler in Rust (parse → check → WASM codegen), plus LSP bits Language surface is deliberately small — enough for frames, entities, and host calls, not a general OS language yet Open the IDE, hit Run (⌘/Ctrl+Enter). There are tutorials and a platformer example in-repo. Repo: https://github.com/AJpro774/Juno I’d love feedback on the language surface, the WASM entity-script ABI, and whether the IDE feels usable for small 2D/3D prototypes.

Is TypeScript Really Worth Learning?
When I first started learning TypeScript, I honestly didn't understand the hype.
